cards.text: Paul, the apostle, is writing a letter to the church in Corinth (1 Corinthians 1:1-2). He just asked them whether they want him to come with a rod, or in love and with a gentle spirit (1 Corinthians 4:21). Now he turns to a report about them: there's sexual immorality among them, and a man has his father's wife.

cards.question: Paul says this kind of sexual immorality isn't tolerated even among ___.
A man in the Corinthian church has his father's wife. How does Paul say the Corinthians are acting about it?

cards.text: Paul says they should have been stricken with grief instead. That's like the smoke alarm SCREAMING and everybody in the kitchen standing around bragging about how good the place smells.

cards.question: Paul says the church should have removed the man who has his father's wife from their ___.

cards.text: Paul isn't in Corinth, but he says he's present with them in spirit even though he's absent in body. Me before my first batch is the exact OPPOSITE: body at the oven, spirit still back on the snooze button.

cards.question: Paul says he'll wait until he gets to Corinth to pronounce judgment on the man who has his father's wife.

cards.text: When they're assembled in the name of the Lord Jesus, with Paul there in spirit and the power of the Lord Jesus, they're to hand this man over to Satan for the destruction of the flesh. That's heavy, friend, but Paul gives a reason.

cards.question: Paul says the man is handed over to Satan for a reason. What does Paul want for the man's spirit on the Day of the Lord?

cards.text: Paul tells them their boasting is not good. Then he pulls an example straight out of the KITCHEN, and friend, I just hopped so high my gold base left the ground.

cards.question: Paul says a little leaven works through the whole batch of dough.

cards.text: So Paul says to get rid of the old leaven, so they can be a new unleavened batch, as they really are. Out it goes, like the dough I kept saying I'd use "tomorrow" for THREE weeks.

cards.question: Paul says Christ has been sacrificed. Which feast's lamb does Paul call Christ?

cards.text: So Paul says let's keep the feast, but not with the old bread, leavened with malice and wickedness. Friend, you could pour EVERY sprinkle in my bakery on that loaf and it still wouldn't help.

cards.question: The old bread is leavened with malice and wickedness. What does Paul say the unleavened bread for the feast is of?

cards.text: Next, Paul brings up an earlier letter where he told the Corinthians not to associate with sexually immoral people. Now he spells out what he meant, and friend, every one of us has sent that second text that starts "Okay, let me explain."

cards.question: Paul meant the Corinthians should stay away from every sexually immoral person in the world.

cards.text: Paul says he wasn't including the sexually immoral, the greedy, swindlers or idolaters of this world, or they'd have to leave this world. Friend, it took an ANGEL to get me out of one junk drawer.

cards.question: Paul's earlier letter said not to associate with sexually immoral people. Who does Paul now say he means?

answers.text: Anyone who claims to be a brother but is immoral or greedy
Anyone outside the church who is immoral or greedy
Anyone in Corinth who has never heard of Jesus

cards.text: Paul names exactly who he means: someone who's sexually immoral or greedy, an idolater or a verbal abuser, a drunkard or a swindler. Friend, my topping jars aren't labeled that clearly, and I named those after my KIDS.

cards.question: Paul says that with someone who claims to be a brother but is sexually immoral or greedy, an idolater or a verbal abuser, a drunkard or a swindler, do not even ___ with him.

cards.text: Then Paul asks what business it is of his to judge those outside the church, and whether the Corinthians aren't to judge those inside. Same reason I scrub my OWN counters every night and have never once flown off this planet to scrub somebody else's.

cards.question: Paul says God will judge those outside the church.
Paul ends with a command for the church about the wicked man. What is it?

answers.text: Pray for him day and night
Send him to Paul at once

rule.text: He calls the baker "baker" or "friend," and talks to one baker at a time. Never "my baker," "kids" or "sweetie."

findings.problem: The phrase "this kind of sexual immorality" points back to card 1, which is no longer visible. The question itself does not explain that a man in the Corinthian church has his father's wife.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: Nothing in the opening card gives the baker a basis for choosing "pagans" over "soldiers" or "priests." The blank asks for an unseen word from the verse rather than a meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: By explaining that Paul was not including immoral or greedy people "of this world," this card rules out both wrong answers on card 4: people outside the church and people in Corinth who have never heard of Jesus. That leaves the correct answer before verse 11 is introduced.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.
